name: Direct Lake Semantic Model + Report
description: Create a native Direct Lake model over existing compatible Delta tables, verify query readiness, and create an empty report bound to it. Routes schema-less sources and authored models to explicit alternatives; real report authoring remains a separate PBIR workflow.
prerequisites: Authenticated caller with permission to create models/reports in the target workspace and read every source data item, including cross-workspace sources.
An active compatible capacity and a real, populated Delta table. A SQL view is not a Delta-table source.
The native path below is live-validated on a schema-enabled lakehouse. For a schema-less lakehouse, choose the generator alternative deliberately; do not silently change the binding after a failure.

variables.MODEL_NAME: Name for the new model; choose an available name before creating it.
variables.REPORT_NAME: Name for the new empty report; choose an available name before creating it.
variables.SOURCE_WS_ID: Source lakehouse workspace ID; may equal WS_ID.
variables.LH_ID: Existing source lakehouse ID. Inspect its properties.defaultSchema and actual Delta tables first.
variables.ONELAKE_TABLE_URL: Canonical HTTPS OneLake DFS URL for the selected table, for example https://onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/$SOURCE_WS_ID/$LH_ID/Tables/dbo/$TABLE_NAME. Use the actual source schema; repeat --one-lake-table for additional tables (maximum 100).
variables.TABLE_NAME: Actual model table name discovered after creation. Substitute it in the DAX example, escaping any apostrophe as two apostrophes.
variables.SM_ID: Capture data.id from model creation; --query id -o plain extracts the payload ID for chaining.
variables.REPORT_ID: Capture data.id from report creation. It is an empty bound report, not a finished dashboard.

steps.description: Inspect the source's schema support and readiness. Do not equate an accepted provisioning request with a usable table.
Choose existing Delta tables. URL syntax validation alone cannot prove table existence, compatible schemas, source access, or data availability.
Preview with --dry-run, then create the native model and capture SM_ID. Do not supply --connection, --file, or --definition in this mode. This path does not need client-side SQL/TDS schema discovery.
Request framing when needed, after reviewing capacity consumption. refresh_triggered means accepted, not completed; do not submit repeated refreshes while waiting.

Poll the new refresh at a bounded interval/deadline until Completed. Stop on Failed or a deadline; inspect details rather than blindly resubmitting. A pre-existing completed refresh is not proof the new one finished.

Inspect the inferred model tables and storage modes, and choose TABLE_NAME. Inspect columns, measures, and relationships before designing visuals; do not assume inferred tables form a complete business model.
Verify a real DAX read before wiring a report. Allow bounded readiness polling after successful framing; permission, schema, and query errors need diagnosis, not arbitrary retries.

Preview with --dry-run, then create an empty report bound to the model and capture REPORT_ID. For a model in another workspace, also pass --semantic-model-workspace with that model's workspace ID. This does not author pages or visuals.

Verify definition.pbir references the intended model. For a real report with visuals, continue with context workflow report-authoring; inspect the stored format before attempting enhanced-PBIR-only editing.

generated_onelake.when: Choose schema-aware, definition-backed generation, including the schema-less lakehouse case. This example creates the model in the source workspace.
generated_onelake.notes: The generator reads the SQL analytics endpoint over TDS and needs SQL-audience credentials. Source schema synchronization may lag. It requests framing unless --no-refresh is supplied; inspect refresh/query readiness rather than assuming creation proves readiness. Switching from native creation to this path is an explicit choice.

authored_model.when: A complete authored model folder already exists, including its expressions, partitions, and definition.pbism.
authored_model.notes: Use --definition for the whole folder. --file accepts one model file only, not repeated files. Preserve the authored data-source expressions; do not blindly add --connection.

empty_model.when: An empty starting point is explicitly wanted. It contains no selected source tables and is not an analytics-ready model.

tips: Native --one-lake-table creation, definition-backed generate --storage-mode onelake, and authored definition import are different paths, not interchangeable flags.

A schema-less native source can fail with DirectLakeSchemaError because the service assumes dbo. Review source compatibility and explicitly select an alternative; URL validity is not a readiness guarantee.
Direct Lake does not import a copy of the source data, but framing/refresh and query readiness still matter.

A blank report created with --semantic-model is not a finished report. For pages and visuals use report scaffold, validate the resulting PBIR folder, then report create --definition with --dataset for rebinding.
Never use --allow-purge-data, takeover, ownership transfer, or a new connection as an automatic retry workaround.
